transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… thanks. I guess the main thing is at work I’ve been having trouble staying at my workstation. I process insurance claims, and even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and get through the reviews, I keep getting up during the day. It’s not like I’m trying to avoid work, exactly… I just find myself leaving my desk more than I probably should. I figured it might be worth talking to someone about, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed this same kind of difficulty staying in one place or focusing on tasks in other parts of your life, like at home or in social situations?

Mostly I’ve noticed it at work, honestly. That’s kind of what made me come in. I’m supposed to stay at my workstation and get through the claim reviews, and I know that, but I keep finding myself getting up during the day more than I should.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just wandering around all day or anything… it’s just enough that I’ve started to worry it’s becoming a problem.
When you're at your workstation, do you find yourself fidgeting, feeling restless, or having trouble focusing even when you're sitting down?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t think it’s super obvious, or I hope it isn’t. But in trainings or longer team meetings, I do catch myself bouncing my leg a lot, or clicking my pen, shifting around in the chair—stuff like that. I’m usually trying to look like I’m paying attention and being professional, but I guess I’m kind of restless even when I’m sitting there.
Have you ever noticed yourself feeling restless or having trouble staying in one place in situations outside of work, like when you're at home relaxing or in social settings?

I guess I’m not as sure about outside of work. The thing I’ve really noticed—the thing that made me think I should come in—is more at my workstation. I’ll be doing claim reviews, and even though I know I’m supposed to just stay there and finish them, I keep getting up during the day.

I don’t know if that answers your question exactly… I just don’t want to overstate it, because work is where it feels most obvious to me.
Can you think of any times when you’ve felt this same restlessness or need to get up and move around—maybe when you're at home watching TV or sitting in a meeting, for example?

Yeah… I mean, the clearest example is still work, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the main thing that pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and just finish my claim reviews.

It’s not like I’m trying to avoid the work, or be difficult… I just notice I’m out of my seat more than I probably should be. Does that make sense?
Can you recall any specific times outside of work—like when you're at home or in a social setting—where you've felt the same kind of restlessness or need to get up and move around?

Honestly, outside of work I’m having a harder time coming up with a clear example. I don’t want to just say yes if I’m not sure.

The thing I keep coming back to is at work—like when I’m supposed to be at my workstation finishing claim reviews, I’ll keep getting up during the day even though I know I should probably just stay seated and get through them. That’s the main thing I’ve really noticed. Is that still useful to tell you, even if I can’t think of a good home or social example?
When you're at work and you get up from your workstation, is it usually because you feel distracted or unable to focus on the claim reviews, or is it more about feeling physically restless?

I think it’s more that I just… end up getting up, even when I know I’m supposed to stay at my workstation and finish the claim reviews. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m bouncing off the walls or anything, but I do leave my seat more than I probably should during the day.

I’m not always sure how to label it—whether it’s distraction or restlessness exactly—but the behavior is that I keep getting up when I know I should stay put. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Can you think of any situations at home, while doing chores or relaxing, where you’ve felt that same urge to get up, move around, or struggle to focus on the task at hand?

At home, I’m not sure I have a great example, to be honest. I don’t want to force it if I’m not really noticing it there.

The clearest thing is still at work—when I’m supposed to stay at my workstation and get through the claim reviews, I keep finding myself getting up during the day. I know I should just stay put and finish them, but I end up leaving my seat more than I probably should. I’m sorry if that’s not exactly what you’re asking about with home situations, but that’s the one that really stands out to me.
Can you remember any times when you’ve been relaxing at home, like watching TV or reading, where you’ve felt the same kind of restlessness or need to get up and move around?

I’m honestly not sure I can point to that happening while I’m watching TV or reading at home. I don’t want to say it does if I’m not really remembering it clearly.

The thing I do know is that at work, I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews. That’s really the main reason I thought I should come in. I know that’s not exactly the home example you’re asking for, but it’s the clearest one for me.
When you're at home trying to relax, like when you're watching TV or using your phone, do you ever find it hard to sit still or stay focused on what you're doing?

I don’t think so, not in a way I’ve really noticed. Like, if I’m watching TV or on my phone, I might shift around like anyone would, but I wouldn’t say I’m getting up over and over or feeling like I can’t sit still.

At least, nothing is coming to mind clearly. I don’t want to overstate it just to give an answer. Is that okay?
When you're doing something at home that requires sitting and focusing, like filling out forms or helping someone with paperwork, do you ever notice yourself getting restless or needing to get up?

I can’t really think of a home paperwork example clearly. I mean, if I’m filling something out at home, I might take a break, but I’m not sure it’s the same thing.

The part I keep coming back to is at work. I’m supposed to stay at my workstation and finish claim reviews, and I just keep getting up during the day, even though I know I should stay put. I know I’ve said that already, sorry—I just don’t want to make up a home example if that’s not really what I’ve noticed.
Can you think of any times in school or childhood when you had trouble sitting still or staying focused, even if it was in a different setting like a classroom?

Yeah… I mean, looking back, I guess it wasn’t totally brand new. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I did okay in school overall, but in elementary school teachers would write things like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets or miss instructions.

I remember needing reminders to finish classwork sometimes too. At the time I think everyone just framed it as me being capable but not always following through, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Can you recall any specific situations in the past six months, outside of work and school, where you had trouble staying seated or focusing on a task—like during meals, social events, or hobbies?

Honestly, outside of work and school, I’m having a hard time thinking of a clear example. Like meals or hobbies… nothing really stands out where I’m obviously unable to stay seated.

The main thing that made me feel like I should come in is still at work. I keep getting up from my workstation during the day when I’m supposed to stay there and finish claim reviews. I know that’s not exactly what you asked, but that’s the situation I can point to without guessing. Is that okay?

Can you think of any situations in the past six months when you were not at work, such as running errands, waiting in line, or sitting in a car for a while, where you felt a strong urge to move around or found it very hard to stay seated?

I’m trying to think of errands or waiting in line, and nothing really clear comes to mind. I don’t want to say yes just to fit the question.

The clearest thing is still work, honestly. I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish the claim reviews. That’s the main thing that made me think I should come in. Is that still useful to tell you, even if it’s not outside work?

When you're at your workstation and supposed to be focusing on claim reviews, do you find it hard to stay focused — like getting distracted easily or having trouble finishing what you start — even if you're not getting up?

Yeah… that does happen. I mean, I can usually get back to it, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m completely unable to work, but if people near me start talking about another claim, or I suddenly remember some random errand I need to do, my attention kind of slides off what I’m reading.

Then I’ll realize I didn’t really absorb that section and I have to reread the same part a few times. It’s frustrating because I’m sitting there and trying to focus, but my brain just sort of… goes somewhere else. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
When you're trying to focus on a task, do you often feel worried or anxious about things unrelated to the task, like something bad happening or making a mistake?

I don’t think so, not in a big way. I mean, I can worry about doing something wrong sometimes, like anyone would, but I haven’t really noticed that being the main thing pulling me off task.

It feels less like I’m sitting there scared something bad will happen, and more like my mind just drifts or gets pulled by something else. But if I’m misunderstanding what you mean, I can try to think about it differently.

Outside of work, have you ever noticed any situations—like being with friends, spending time with family, or participating in hobbies—where your restlessness or difficulty focusing has caused problems or seemed to interfere with what you were doing?

I’m not sure I can point to a clear example outside of work. Like with friends or family, I don’t think anyone has really complained about me being restless or not paying attention.

Maybe I zone out sometimes during a movie or if people are talking for a long time, but that feels kind of normal, so I don’t want to overstate it. I guess the problems I’ve noticed most are still at work. If there’s a specific kind of situation you mean, I can try to think harder.
